evidence: Cic. Phil. 2.105: tē inquilīnō (nōn enim dominō)
Suet. Ner. 44.2: inquilīnōs prīvātārum aedium atque īnsulārum, tenants of private houses and of blocks of flats
terms.comment: One who lives in a place not his own (Lewis & Short), set against the owner, dominus.

terms.gloss: the one who rents; a tenant of a house or farm
evidence: Caes. BC 3.21.1: mercēdēs habitātiōnum annuās conductōribus dōnāvit
Cic. Att. 12.32.2: conductōrēs quī sint et quantī, who the tenants are and what they pay
terms.comment: The party who condūcit, rents (see rent, pay to use); also one who hires workers (see employer).

evidence: Cic. Caecin. 94: quī colōnus habuit conductum dē Caesenniā fundum, who as tenant farmer had rented the farm from Caesennia
terms.comment: Properly a farmer; one who farms land that he rents.

phrases.latin: essedās trānscurrentēs pōnō et fabrum inquilīnum et serrārium vīcīnum
phrases.english: I count in the carriages rattling past, the carpenter who lodges in the building and the sawyer next door

phrases.latin: Partem etiam cēnsūs omnēs ōrdinēs cōnferre jussit et īnsuper inquilīnōs prīvātārum aedium atque īnsulārum pēnsiōnem annuam repraesentāre fiscō
phrases.english: He also ordered every class to contribute part of its property, and tenants of private houses and of blocks of flats to pay a year’s rent to the treasury at once

phrases.latin: At vērō tē inquilīnō (nōn enim dominō) personābant omnia vōcibus ēbriōrum
phrases.english: But with you as tenant (for you were not the owner) the whole house rang with drunken voices
